Plain-English schedule

    When both day-of-month and day-of-week are restricted, standard cron runs when either matches (OR logic).

    📖 How to use

    1. For each of the five fields, choose a mode: every, specific values, range or step.
    2. Fill in the values for list, range or step modes.
    3. Read the cron expression and the plain-English description.
    4. Check the next three scheduled run times below.

    ❓ Frequently asked questions

    Does it support every cron feature?

    No. This builder supports every (*), specific value lists, ranges and steps — the most common cron syntax. Special characters like L, W and # are not supported.

    Are the next run times exact?

    The next run times are found by scanning forward minute by minute (up to a year ahead), so they are exact for the schedule you built — but they are labeled approximate because month lengths and daylight-saving quirks vary by system.

    How do day-of-month and day-of-week combine?

    Standard cron OR logic: if you restrict both day-of-month and day-of-week, the job runs when either one matches.
